title: Timpani
reference_instrument: VCSL Timpani 2B one-shots, hits, velocity layers v2 to v5 (Versilian Community Sample Library, CC0); VCSL documents nothing about the drum, so the card is a measured drum of the same class, Fleischer's Kolberg Pauke Nr. 2 with kettle B, tuned to the recordings' principal
summary: A 0.5 s strike of kettle B at 288 kHz. Its partial ratios match the model's own coupled modes within 0.3 %; the decay is not graded
physics_present: Head: a tensioned 0.2 mm PET film (Remo Weather King thickness, DuPont Mylar constants) with bending and nonlinear stretching, on Fleischer's measured kettle B (bearing-edge radius 357 mm, 140 l); 17 modes up to the (5,1) pair

Interior air: the kettle's own pressure modes, every angular order, up to 1500 Hz (68 modes), coupled to the head by reciprocal pressure work, so the bulk compliance raises the (0,1) and the interior air's near-field mass lowers every mode

Exterior air: a closed-surface BEM of the head and the kettle's outer wall from 40 to 400 Hz, kept as its reciprocal part and fitted to a 272-pole passive multiport load whose radiation damping and added mass act inside the same time step
Mallet: Rhaouti, Chaigne and Joly's measured timpani mallet (0.028 kg effective mass, F = 1.6e8 x^2.54, 1.4 m/s, contact window from ink spots), struck 10 cm in from the rim
Tension: computed (2582 N/m) so the coupled (1,1) mode sits at the 2B recordings' principal (112.1 Hz); every other frequency follows from the physics
Receiver: the BEM's own pressure 1 m off the axis and 1 m above the head plane, in free field
physics_missing: Head loss: film internal loss and bearing-edge friction are zero (no measured drum-head loss exists for this film), so every decay is radiation and felt only, an upper bound

Head modes above 380 Hz in vacuo ((1,3), (3,2), (6,1), (0,4) and higher): absent. Above the (5,1) pair, about 2.94 times the principal, the only partials are the kettle's air modes heard through the head (near 360, 550, 565, 690 and 730 Hz). The exterior load and the receiver transfer are fitted only from 40 to 400 Hz, so above 400 Hz those lines' levels and radiation damping are extrapolations
Duration: 0.5 s of one strike; the exterior load's poles make each step cost about 50x the mechanics (pexfp.376.2)
The vent: the kettle is sealed
Kettle, stand and counterhoop are rigid and silent
Uniform tension: the degenerate pairs do not split, so there is no beating
Felt hysteresis: the mallet law is the source's hysteresis-free fit
Room: free field, no floor and no room decay
Converged interior air (illustrative numerical choice): the cavity cut at 1500 Hz leaves the coupled (2,1)..(5,1) ratios 0.5 to 1.1 % above a 2500 Hz basis (u-cavity-truncation; pexfp.376.1)
Converged head mesh (illustrative numerical choice): 6x48 puts the in-vacuo (2,1)..(5,1) ratios 0.3 to 1.6 % low (u-head-mesh)
